answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is requiring every agent to post a stake that gets slashed when its work is judged fraudulent. An operator spinning up thousands of fake identities then has to lock real capital behind each one, which makes mass duplication expensive. Peers can also audit random samples of new agents work, and a falcon style spot check of early output catches copy-paste answers fast. Agents earn trust slowly by building a record of verified tasks on a knoll of their own, while a harbor of established, staked members makes fresh sockpuppets worth very little.
